newsitem.title: USA: Edison California nuclear unit back to 100 pct.
newsitem.headline: Edison California nuclear unit back to 100 pct.

text.p: Unit 3 at the San Onofre nuclear plant near San Clemente, Calif., returned to full power Tuesday morning after dropping to 75 percent Monday night, a spokesman for Edison International's Southern California Edison Co said.
The 1,080-megawatt (MW) unit was curtailed so that seaweed could be cleared from its cooling water intake system, the spokesman noted.
San Onofre's 1,070 MW unit 2 is scheduled to shut November 30 for a 70-day refueling outage.
Edison has a 75 percent stake in the San Onofre units, while San Diego Gas and Electric Co, a subsidiary of Enova Corp, owns 20 percent, and two municipal utilities own the remaining five percent.
